[[File:Crystal_Cave_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|250px|Lightsaber crystals]]
{{Quote|The crystal is, by itself, the power source of the weapon. Like the Force user, the crystal is attuned to the Force. Without that attunement, the crystal is just a rock. And while a non-Force user could probably ignite and wield a lightsaber, the crystal is needed to be properly attuned to the Force. But for a Jedi, the lightsaber becomes more: it is a manifestation of a Jedi's connection to the Force.|[[Jaden Korr]]|<ref name="Riptide">[[Riptide (novel)|''Riptide'']]</ref>}}
'''Lightsaber crystals''' or '''jewels''', also known as '''focusing crystals''' or '''kyber crystals''', were a variety of [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]], gems, stones, or other objects that were used as the energy source of a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].

At the heart of every lightsaber was a single crystal that resonated to produce the efficient, powerful blade. While the most common crystals used in the process were from the [[Adega system/Legends|Adega system]], [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]] and [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] (in the so-called [[Crystal Cave (Dantooine)|Crystal Cave]]), [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] used a variety of crystals to produce various colors, effects and unique abilities. [[Focus|Some crystals]] could even enhance the [[The Force/Legends|Force]] skills of a particular user. Other gems, such as colored crystals or diamonds, were used exclusively for prismatic effects. However, not all lightsaber focusing crystals were actually 'crystals'. Plenty of Jedi or Sith used a different material or substance in place of a crystal, such as physical remains, shards of glass and even special micro machinery.

During the [[Dark Wars]], many lightsabers were created using [[Kunda stone]]s,<ref name="kotorii">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> a natural geologic formation from the planet [[Kadril]],<ref name="kadril">"[[Planet of Kadril]]"</ref> in place of crystals. These stones boasted numerous practical applications in medicine and communications; however, when added to other focusing crystals, they produced a broader beam.<ref name="kotorii" />

==Preparation==
{{Quote|The heart of the lightsaber, the crystal is.|[[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="The Gathering (episode)">{{TCW|The Gathering (episode)}}</ref>}}
[[File:FDCR_ChV_Gear_and_Equipment.png|thumb|left|250px|A Jedi constructs his lightsaber during the Galactic Civil War.]]
Before placing the crystal in the lightsaber, the Jedi or Sith had to imbue it with the Force. To do this, the Force-user was required to meditate on the crystal for many days. [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] meditated on his crystal in [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Ben Kenobi's]] [[Ben Kenobi's home/Legends|home]] with only [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] to keep him company.<ref name="Shadows of the Empire novel">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

While the Jedi mostly used natural crystals, the Sith usually used red-hued [[Synthetic lightsaber crystal/Legends|synthetic crystals]].<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> However, Luke Skywalker created his lightsaber using a synthetic crystal, because he had no access to natural crystals on Tatooine.<ref name="Shadows of the Empire novel" /> Sith-made synthetic crystals created a slightly more powerful blade when energized by the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Sith lightsaber blades could occasionally "break" the blade of a Jedi saber.<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] had [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] use a special furnace to make his own crystals. Maul worked constantly for several days to make the four crystals needed for his [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]]. Their creation required intense concentration, as Darth Maul had to use the Force not only to make them the proper shape and to ensure that the crystals were free from impurities, but also to keep himself alive for the long time it took in the blistering heat of the furnace. Maul was particularly proud of this achievement and believed it to be an example of the Sith's superiority over the Jedi.<ref name="Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> However, Sidious did not make his subsequent apprentices&mdash;[[Dooku/Legends|Tyranus]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Vader]]&mdash;create their crystals in such a manner, instead supplying them himself.<ref name="AotC:VD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref><ref name="DarkLord">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

[[File:Initiate_with_crystal_FDNP.png|thumb|327x327px|A human force-sensitive holds his lightsaber crystal after completing [[Gathering/Legends|The Gathering]].]]
Luke Skywalker, who had decided to create his lightsaber crystal instead of using a natural one, also used a special furnace he found in Obi-Wan Kenobi's home to prepare his crystal.<ref name="Shadows of the Empire novel" />

The Jedi Order had an [[Cleanse|advanced technique]] that allowed, in case of need, the cleaning of synthetic crystals made by dark-side users from the hate of their former owners. In [[41 ABY]], Jaden Korr, who had lost [[Jaden Korr's second lightsaber|his second lightsaber]], used the Force to banish the dark side from the red crystal of a Dark Jedi he had killed. Through meditation, he was able to remove all traces of the dark side and imbue the crystal with the light side, turning the Dark Jedi's lightsaber into a [[Jaden Korr's third lightsaber|yellow-bladed Jedi weapon]].<ref name="Riptide" />

==Significance of colors==
{{Quote|Blue is the color of the Jedi Guardian. This Jedi battles against the forces of evil and the dark side. They focus more on combat training and use of the lightsaber. Yellow is the color of the Jedi Sentinel. This Jedi ferrets out deceit and injustice, bringing it to light. They focus less on combat and more on other skills and abilities. Green is the color of the Jedi Consular. This Jedi seeks to bring balance to the universe. They mediate between other groups, using their powers to end conflict and preserve peace.|[[Dorak]]|<ref name="KotOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
In [[3956 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' says that the events of ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' happened in [[3956 BBY]].</ref> [[Dorak]] told [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] that [[Jedi Guardian/Legends|Jedi Guardians]] used blue lightsaber crystals, [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Jedi Sentinels]] used yellow lightsaber crystals, and that [[Jedi Consular]]s used green lightsaber crystals.<ref name="KotOR" /> [[Crix Sunburris]], [[Sabla-Mandibu]], and [[Morrit Ch'gally/Legends|Morrit Ch'gally]] said the same in [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]].<ref name="jedipath">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

From the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]] until the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] almost exclusively used [[Ilum crystal/Legends|Ilum crystals]], which were always either blue or green, for lightsaber construction, resulting in almost all [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] wielding either blue or green lightsabers.<ref name="POTJ">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Starting with the reign of the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] over the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]],<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] used [[Synthetic lightsaber crystal/Legends|synthetic lightsaber crystals]], resulting in their lightsabers being red.<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual" />

==Types of lightsaber crystals==
{{Quote|One of the other crucial pieces is a focusing crystal. The most powerful and sought-after gems are rare Kaiburr crystals. However, though lightsabers are powerful weapons, their design is so flexible that practically any kind of crystal can be used.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to his students on making a lightsaber|<ref name="Young Jedi Knights: Lightsabers">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Lightsabers]]''</ref>}}
There were a number of different stones, minerals and crystals that could be used in the construction of a lightsaber. Some jewels created different colors and effects in the lightsabers in which they were placed. Often, the rarer the crystal, the more powerful its effects on a lightsaber.<ref name="KotOR" />

==List of crystal colors==
Lightsaber crystals could be compressed, resulting in a pulsating blade, or they could be unstable, resulting in a core which swirled and sparkled.<ref name="TFU" />

Lightsaber crystals of different hues could also be used in the same lightsaber to make a new blade color; for example, [[Galen Marek]] used [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota's]] green crystal along with [[Kento Marek|his father's]] deep blue crystal to create an aqua blue blade.<ref name="TFU" />

*Black-Silver<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic" />

==Behind the scenes==
The earliest concept of the Kyber crystal, the "Kiber Crystal", was conceived as a plot device in the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second draft]] of the original [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']] movie, similar to the Ring of Power in [[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien's]] fantasy trilogy, [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings|''The Lord of the Rings'']].<ref name="Making of Star Wars">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> In one of [[George Lucas]]' initial notes for ''[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|Empire Strikes Back]]'' is written "Kiber crystal in sword?".<ref name="The Making of The Empire Strikes Back">''[[The Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> Crystals first appeared in actual ''Star Wars'' material simply as an embedded decoration on the lightsaber hilt in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''A New Hope'' novelization]].<ref name="E4n">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> Aside from this single instance, there are no crystals mentioned in the [[original trilogy]] or its novelizations.<ref name="E4n" /><ref name="E5n">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="E6n">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> 

The first account of crystals in general being an internal component of lightsabers was given in ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'', published by [[West End Games]] in 1987. First identified as "jewels," one to three of these multifaceted stones determine the blade's length, with natural jewels producing the best sabers, although synthetic ones can be forged by a Jedi using "a small furnace and a few basic elements." 

The endnotes to the 1991 ''[[Dark Empire]]'' series by [[Tom Veitch]] reiterate the concept of lightsaber jewels from the ''Sourcebook'', and in later editions expand on and revise it, with the introduction of the earliest known examples for lightsaber construction being natural "Ilum crystals," mostly found in the Adega system.<ref name="Dark Empire endnotes">[[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]] {{C|Such an Old Lightsword is Not a Worthy Weapon For You!}} {{C|[[1995]] second edition}}</ref> First discovered by ancient Jedi, Ilum crystals were used in combination with more common jewelled stones to focus the spontaneous energy bursts they emit, and were commonly known as "Adegan crystals," the namesake of their primary source. A planet named Ilum was introduced in the 2001 novel ''[[Jedi Quest: Path to Truth]]'' by [[Jude Watson]], the namesake of Ilum crystals with which it was abundant, and supplanted the Adega system as their primary source in continuity.

In ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', players must "tune" lightsaber crystals to themselves before they may use them in a lightsaber. Once tuned, the crystal can only be used by that player, and only in lightsabers created by that player.<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies" /> In ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', players are able to gain lightsaber crystals to use with their lightsabers.<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic" />

"[[A Test of Strength]]," the seventh episode from the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', first completely identified "kyber" crystals as a component of lightsaber construction.<ref name="A Test of Strength">{{TCW|A Test of Strength}}</ref> Soon after, an article published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]] established that "kyber crystals" and "lightsaber crystals" were exchangeable terms.<ref name="Encyclopedia">{{SWE|technology|lightsaber-crystals|lightsaber crystals}}</ref> This was later made even more evident with the [[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]], which identified several variety of crystals, such as ("Ilum crystal" or "Krayt dragon pearl") under the umbrella of "kyber crystals".<ref name="FoD">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>
